text: Damping Runge–Kutta iterations for steady solutions Interpret multistage pseudo-time iterations as smoothers for a steady residual. A Jameson–Schmidt–Turkel-family example connects stage coefficients, stability polynomials, nonlinear order, high-frequency damping and preconditioning. The target is R(U)=0, not a physical-time trajectory For a discrete steady Euler/Navier–Stokes residual R, iterate an artificial ODE in pseudo time τ toward its root. Here R is the conservative residual divided by cell volume. The step is a pseudo-time step; the aim is an adequately converged residual and steady observables, not an accurate physical transient. Stability and high-frequency damping are different For linearized residual modes, the iteration multiplier is a stability polynomial. |ℛ|≤1 prevents growth, but |ℛ| near one barely damps error. A multigrid smoother seeks small maximum amplification μ on frequencies H not representable on the coarse grid. For a purely decaying z=−2 mode, this four-stage polynomial gives ℛ=1/3, while near-zero low-frequency modes decay slowly. Pushing the step to a stability boundary does not maximize damping or minimize time to convergence. Residual smoothing, preconditioning and multigrid Residual smoothing is a separate spatial filtering operation, not the choice of RK stage coefficients. With dimensionless centered D₂ on a uniform periodic grid and ε≥0, the example below attenuates high-frequency residuals. An invertible filter retains the residual root but changes the iteration spectrum. Low-Mach preconditioning changes acoustic/convective scales, local stepping changes per-cell iteration increments, and coarse correction treats errors poorly reduced by the smoother. Combined iterations still require boundary/variable-coefficient/nonnormality analysis and must be distinguished from physical-time integration. Measure residuals, steady observables and work Measure Fourier-mode damping on a manufactured Poisson-type problem and compare with μ. For compressible flow track true residuals scaled by conservative component and steady quantities such as forces, mass flow and conservation balances. When smoothing residuals, also display the original unsmoothed residual. Report residual evaluations and linear-solve work, final errors and termination reasons, not only stage/cycle counts. Compare methods at the same steady solution and tolerance. This chapter supplies algorithmic reading, not a dedicated Jameson solver or new flow-validation results. Publication scope and related entries This is reading on steady multistage RK iteration. Existing classical RK4, dual-time and multigrid examples do not implement or validate a complete Jameson-type compressible solver. No dedicated solver or new measured results are added.
